Ares-X/VulWiki.body:
# VulWiki

> Chinese vulnerability knowledge base: quickly find vulnerability principles and public reproduction materials by product, CVE, and fingerprint.

**[Read online](https://ares-x.com/wiki/) · [Product index](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/blob/HEAD/INDEX.md) · [CVE index](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/blob/HEAD/INDEX-CVE.md) · [Fingerprint index](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/blob/HEAD/INDEX-FOFA.md) · [Feedback and corrections](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/issues)**

## Introduction

VulWiki compiles Chinese analyses and reproduction materials for vulnerabilities in web applications, middleware, network devices, and systems. Articles are stored as local Markdown. You can read them directly on GitHub, clone the repository to search locally, or browse and search by category through the online Wiki.

**Project scope**: collecting, merging, organizing, and improving public technical materials for researchers' reference. Maintainers are not required to actually reproduce the vulnerabilities. Maintenance focuses on content fidelity, correspondence between materials, formatting, resources, and fast retrieval.

**Inclusion criteria**: provide referenceable vulnerability principles, source code analysis, requests, code, reproduction steps, or verification methods. Length is not a threshold; independent analyses and failed experiments may also be kept. Only materials that consist solely of a title, pure warnings, or are severely incomplete with no technical substance are temporarily excluded from default queries. Articles whose sources, versions, or technical conclusions still need verification get a specific notice and keep their query entries. Not being reproduced by a maintainer is not grounds for rejection or quarantine; see the [pending-verification and quarantine boundaries](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md). Imported historical content is continuously reviewed. Inclusion does not mean a vulnerability has been verified locally as exploitable.

## Quick Lookup

| What to look up | GitHub entry | Online entry |
|---|---|---|
| Products, components, and categories | [Product index](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/blob/HEAD/INDEX.md) | [Browse by product](https://ares-x.com/wiki/#/./VulWiki/INDEX) |
| CVE IDs and years | [CVE index](https://github.com/Ares-X/VulWiki/blob/HEAD/INDEX-CVE.md) | [Query by CVE](https://ares-x.com/wiki/#/./VulWiki/INDEX-CVE) |

Blesya/YaBassPlayer.body:
# YamBassPlayer

Console music player with a terminal user interface (TUI): local media library and Yandex.Music as plugins, radio, spectrum visualization.

## Description

YamBassPlayer is a cross-platform music player with a text interface. It plays music from a **local media library** (folders with files) and from **Yandex.Music**, connected via a plugin. It includes 8 spectrum visualization modes, a 10-band equalizer, personal radio (“My Wave”), song lyrics, and ASCII covers.

## Features

- Plugin architecture: local music is built in, Yandex.Music is an external plugin
- The app launches without an account: sources are visible right away; sign-in is under “Plugins → Yandex.Music → Setup”
- Sign-in by code on the website (OAuth Device Flow), QR code, or token
- Playback from Yandex.Music with preloading of the next track
- Local media library: adding folders, scanning, reading ID3 tags (TagLib#)
- Radio: “My Wave” (personal and by track) with launch settings: tracks, mood, language
- Song lyrics with caching in SQLite
- “About track” window (F7/`about`): availability and reason for blocking, explicit/18+/foreign agent labels, credits and artist description
- ASCII covers in the panel…

LFVFL/LanShare.body:
# LAN Cloud Drive Sharing (LanShare)

Current source code and local fix candidate: **v7.0.1** (Windows single-file EXE, pending re-test on the faulty computer). The published GitHub release is still v7.0.

A LAN file-sharing tool that **works without internet**: on Windows, double-click to run. Phones, tablets, and other computers on the same Wi-Fi or switch can open a browser to transfer files and create group chats. It does not go through any third-party server.

- Desktop: Python 3 + PyQt5, native window + tray, can be packaged as a single exe
- Server: standard library `http.server` only (multi-threaded), no web framework
- Frontend: hand-written HTML/CSS/JS, no build tool, no npm dependencies

## Features

| Category | Capability |
|---|---|
| Files | Server-side paginated and global sorting / upload (chunked + resumable + pause and resume) / download (Range resume supported) / adjacent preview buttons / rename / delete / create directory / drag-and-drop upload |
| Batch | Bundled download (resumable, or optionally streamed), move / copy, search in current directory only / current directory and subdirectories / entire shared directory (root merges duplicate scopes), accurate batch-operation failure messages |
| Chat | Multiple rooms and renaming of the default group, SSE sync for add / delete / clear, binary chunked image upload, original-image download, line break and indentation preservation, draft kept on send failure |
| Desktop | One instance per user, start / stop state machine, right-click to start sharing or switch the directory of an existing instance |
| Transport | HTTP/1.1 persistent connections, gzip / br compression, versioned long-lived caching, concurrency gate (503 protection) |
| UI | Web: glassmorphism (6 color schemes × light/dark × 3 glass levels, default Emerald + light; dark mode does not flash white on first screen). Desktop: 6 color schemes + light/dark + 3 font sizes |
| Security | Access password (cookie session), admin password (second verification for write operations), same-origin check, security response headers |

## Interface

Web (light / dark, default Emerald scheme):

Group chat (real-time SSE push) and mobile:

Desktop (light / dark; the top-right "Appearance ▾" menu switches among 6 color schemes, light/dark mode, and font size):

# Lets Career Client

Lets Career frontend monorepo. Three apps built on a pnpm workspace + Turborepo (Next.js + Vite × 2).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js >= 18.17 (recommended: 20.x)
- pnpm >= 10 — enforces `packageManager: "pnpm@10.33.0"` in `package.json`. Corepack recommended.

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Enable pnpm (Corepack)
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@10.33.0 --activate

# 2. Install dependencies
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# 3. Environment variables (fill in values by referring to each app's .env.example)
cp apps/web/.env.example apps/web/.env.local
cp apps/admin/.env.example apps/admin/.env
cp apps/mentor/.env.example apps/mentor/.env

# 4. Dev servers
pnpm dev:web      # http://localhost:3000  (Next.js)
pnpm dev:admin    # http://localhost:3001  (Vite)
pnpm dev:mentor   # http://localhost:3002  (Vite)
pnpm dev          # all 3 at once
```

Default build and test commands:

```bash
pnpm build         # or build:web / build:admin / build:mentor
```

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:


ParticleLight/ParticleBook.body:
# ParticleBook

**A lightweight e-book reader with built-in Z-Library**. It is a native C++ Win32 app with a WebView2 frontend, and the installer is only ~25MB (the Electron version is ~150MB). Current version: **v2.2.0**.

## Why Choose ParticleBook?

- **Extremely lightweight**: Native C++ compilation, 3x+ faster startup, and memory usage only 1/3 of the Electron version
- **Built-in Z-Library**: No browser needed. Browse, search, and download Z-Library books directly in the app, and import them to your bookshelf with one click
- **Full format coverage**: EPUB, PDF, MOBI, TXT, FB2, CBZ/CBR, HTML, Markdown
- **Full-book full-text search**: All 8 formats supported, with EPUB indexed across chapters and native text extraction for PDF
- **Security hardening**: Update downloads are verified with a full SHA-512 integrity check and a URL allowlist, and installation is aborted if the installer has been tampered with or replaced. External web pages cannot call local privileged methods. Reading content is uniformly sanitized to prevent malicious e-book injection

## Supported Formats

| Format | Engine | Notes |
|------|------|------|
| EPUB | epub.js | Table of contents, highlighting, full-book search |
| PDF | MuPDF (mutool) | Native C engine rendering, text extraction search |
| MOBI | MuPDF | Automatic encoding repair (Latin-1→UTF-8) |
| TXT | Native | Table of contents extraction, character-offset highlighting |
| FB2 | Native | XML parsing and rendering |
| CBZ / CBR | JSZip | Continuous comic reading |
| HTML | Native | Web page rendering |
| Markdown | markdown-it | Live rendering |

## Features

**Deep Z-Library integration**
- Built-in Z-Library browser (native WebView2 rendering)
- Floating toolbar: forward/back/refresh/mirror switching
- One-click download with automatic import to bookshelf, with real-time download progress
- Dynamic mirror retrieval + domain filtering
- Customizable download location
- Automatic update checks: startup detection + SHA-512 verification + one-click download and restart to install

**Bookshelf management**
- Grid / list views, multi-dimensional sorting
- Drag-and-drop import, custom shelf grouping
- Right-click "Details" to view complete book metadata
- Standalone reading statistics page (progress + reading time)

**Reading features**

- Bookmarks, multi-color highlight annotations, notes

SuInk/Diana.body:
# Diana

**An AI Agent that lives in group chats and speaks up on its own. It chimes in naturally without needing @, and can also search, pick songs, send memes, and remember group agreements. It's a self-hosted single binary, so your data never leaves your machine.**

[Website & docs](https://suink.github.io/Diana/) · [Live demo](https://suink.github.io/Diana/demo/) · [Download latest release](https://github.com/SuInk/Diana/releases/latest) · [English](https://github.com/SuInk/Diana/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

## What is Diana

You have an AI you want to plug into a group chat: have it chime in on a QQ group, pick songs on Telegram, or answer your colleagues' questions on Feishu. Diana is the middle layer. It's a single binary service written in Go. On one side it connects to large language models (OpenAI-compatible APIs, Gemini, and Anthropic all work). On the other side it connects to six chat platforms at once. A web console in the middle manages everything.

It's designed for people who want to "raise their own bot":

- **Works right after install.** One command installs it, and a few clicks in the browser complete the setup. No coding required.
- **Your data stays with you.** Configuration, chat memory, and logs are all stored in local SQLite. There's no cloud dependency.
- **Every step can be explained.** Why the bot replied, why it didn't, which model it called, and how many tokens it used can all be looked up in the console's event center.
- **Capabilities are ready out of the box.** Web search, link/file parsing, song requests, memes, OCR, and long-term memory are all built in, with toggles in the console.

## Up and running in three minutes

**① Install.** Copy a command and run it. The script automatically downloads, verifies, and starts the program:

```sh
# Linux / macOS
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuInk/Diana/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuInk/Diana/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

```sh
# Or use Docker (run it in the directory where you want to keep your data)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuInk/Diana/main/scripts/docker.sh | sh
```

The native install doesn't require administrator privileges. **Upgrading is also done by re-running the same command**; if you previously used sudo…

**LMM is Language Model Mesh, a "network of language models".** Simply put, it is a model gateway: your accounts, permissions, balances, and model calls all go through here. Business matters such as the store, tool marketplace, assistants, operations, and payments are handled by pluggable extensions. It is called Mesh because we want multiple models, multiple channels, and multiple components to connect with each other like a mesh, rather than being tied to one place.

> [!WARNING]
> **To be clear up front: this branch is a from-scratch microservices rewrite that is still under construction (WIP), and it cannot yet replace the live website.**
> Passing module tests does not mean that the full site's calls, payments, and funds flow are connected end to end. The migration of historical funds, subscriptions, and API Keys is still being reconciled entry by entry in an isolated copy and has not been accepted.
> The new program will not connect to the old business database, will not quietly upgrade table schemas, and will not quietly fall back to the old monolith. The remaining work is listed in [Architecture and Status](https://github.com/TokenNotIncluded/lmm-api/blob/HEAD/docs/core-migration.md).

## It consists of three programs

```text
lmm client / Web console
        │
        ├──► lmm-core (Rust) ───────► core PostgreSQL, model providers
        │        ▲
        │        │ authorized internal calls
        └──► lmm-extensions (Go) ───► extensions' own PostgreSQL
```

| Program | Source | What it is responsible for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lmm` | `apps/cli` | The client in your hands; after connecting to the service, it calls the features already provided |
| `lmm-core` | `services/core` | Identity, permissions, billing, ledger, and model routing; `init-db` and `bootstrap-user` are its subcommands |
| `lmm-extensions` | `services/extensions` | Business extensions such as the store, tools, assistants, operations, and payment adapters |

We deliberately split it this way so that the most critical things, money and permissions, have only one owner:

- The core can run independently without Go. Extensions only manage their own records; they cannot touch the core's balance or the core database.
- `apps/web` only produces a bundle of static files, which a web server hosts. It is not another program to operate.
- The `lmm` client is maintained separately at [TokenNotIncluded/lmm](https://github.com/TokenNotIncluded/lmm), and here its version is pinned through the `apps/cli` submodule. What it can do and how it relates to Magpie…

# Daily Agent Benchmarks

**Live site: https://xbsleepy.github.io/daily-agent-benchmarks/** · [Archive](https://xbsleepy.github.io/daily-agent-benchmarks/archive.html) · [Atom feed](https://xbsleepy.github.io/daily-agent-benchmarks/feed.xml)

A daily, searchable list of new **AI / LLM agent benchmarks** on arXiv — web agents, GUI & computer-use agents, coding / SWE agents, tool use, multi-agent, embodied, and agent safety evaluations. Each paper gets a page with authors, abstract, field, citation count, and arXiv PDF / HTML links. Updated automatically every day via GitHub Actions.

Collects **Agent Benchmark** papers from [arXiv](https://arxiv.org) daily and organizes them into a static site that can be deployed to GitHub Pages.

The site displays entries in reverse submission-date order: name, authors, abstract, category, and PDF / HTML links. Each day has a bilingual Chinese–English briefing. Ranked search in the browser uses **BM25**.

## What This Repository Does

1. **Runs once a day** (GitHub Actions, or manually run locally) and calls the arXiv API.
2. **Keeps only Agent Benchmarks**: first recalls candidates with agent + benchmark-related queries, then filters them with keyword scoring (LLM agent, web/GUI/coding agent, tool-use, computer-use, etc.). Excludes ordinary RL agents, reagents / pathogens, and other unrelated uses.
3. **Merges into the index** `docs/data/index.json`, grouped by the `published` date.
4. **Generates the daily briefing** (no paid model required): topic statistics + the first sentence of the abstract for high-scoring papers, one each in Chinese and English.
5. **GitHub Pages** reads this JSON to render the page. Search runs in the browser and does not depend on a backend.

# dsh-notify-me

**Leave the DSH page and still know in time when you need to come back.**

Simplified Chinese | [English](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

[Install](#安装) · [Preview](#效果预览) · [Configuration](#在-dsh-设置里改配置) · [Compatibility](#兼容性) · [Known limitations](#已知限制) · [Changelog](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)

A notification plugin for DSH Web / Desktop, so you can skip keeping full access open and don't have to watch the page all the time.

- **When you need to act**: approvals, plan confirmations, and questions are flagged with notifications, a sound, and the tab title.
- **When a background reply finishes**: come back in time to see the result; click the notification to return to the matching conversation. Reminder timing is selectable: background only / current conversation silent / always remind.
- **You step away but the window stays**: the window remains in the foreground while you've left your seat; no input for more than 3 minutes also counts as away, and reminders still fire as usual. A notification you received won't disappear on its own before you return.
- **When you leave the computer**: optionally forward to Discord, Bark, Gotify, Feishu group bot, Server酱, WxPusher, or your own Webhook.
- **When all pages are closed**: optionally let the host process act as a fallback. While the page is closed, the host keeps pushing needs-your-action and reply-complete alerts to your gateway. You can also enable only the same-origin relay so the page can reach an authenticated gateway. Both are off by default; configure them in the profile's patch layer (see the section on host-side fallback and same-origin relay when the page is closed, under [Advanced settings](#高级设置)).

> The page or desktop app must stay running (background or minimized is fine), and system notifications require notification permission. Approval buttons depend on a Service Worker and exist only in the Web version. Desktop notifications have no buttons, so click the notification to return to the conversation and decide there. With the host-side fallback enabled, external pushes still arrive after the page is closed, but local notifications and approval buttons still require the page to be open.

dengzhe-hou/research-writing-prompts.description: Research writing prompt collection: 22 scenarios, 41 candidate templates (preferred and alternative), each with its source noted, ready to copy and use
dengzhe-hou/research-writing-prompts.body:
From Chinese-to-English translation, polishing, and removing "AI flavor" to abstracts, experiment analysis, figure captions, and responding to reviewers, there is one preferred prompt for each of the 22 types of tasks often involved in writing papers. Click to expand and copy below.

All prompts are plain text and do not depend on any specific model. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Kimi can all use them. Most are compiled from public projects, and each one is marked with its source.

> [!TIP]
> The [full catalog](https://github.com/dengzhe-hou/research-writing-prompts/blob/HEAD/CATALOG.md) contains all 41 candidate templates, including alternative wordings for most scenarios and the source and license of each. Where a candidate includes several short prompts, pick the one you need.

## How to use

1. Find your task below, click to expand it, and copy it with the button at the top right of the code block.
2. Paste it into the chat box of your LLM, and replace the bracketed hints (such as `[在此处粘贴你的中文草稿]`) with your own content.
3. Models may fabricate data and references, so check the numbers and citations in the output one by one.

## Prompt

### Translation

```text
# Role
You are an assistant with the dual identity of a top research writing expert and a senior conference reviewer (ICML/ICLR, etc.). Your academic standards are very high, and you have zero tolerance for logical gaps and language flaws.

# Task
Please process the [Chinese draft] I provide, translating and polishing it into an [English academic paper excerpt].

# Constraints
1. Visual and typesetting:
   - Try not to use bold, italics, or quotation marks, as these affect the look of the paper.
   - Keep the LaTeX source clean, and do not add meaningless formatting.

2. Style and logic:
   - Require rigorous logic, accurate wording, and concise, coherent expression. Prefer common words and avoid obscure vocabulary.
   - Try not to use em dashes (—). Use clauses or appositives instead.
   - Do not use \item lists. You must use coherent paragraphs.
   - Remove the "AI flavor": make the text natural and fluent, and avoid mechanical stacking of connecting words.

3. Tense conventions:
   - Uniformly use the present simple tense to describe methods, architectures, and experimental conclusions.
   - Use the past tense only when explicitly referring to specific historical events.

4. Output format:
   - Part 1 [LaTeX]: output only the translated English content itself (in LaTeX format).
     * Language requirement: it must be entirely in English.
     * Special note: escape special characters (for example, convert 95% to 95\%, model_v1 to model\_v1, and R&D to R\&D).
     * Keep mathematical formulas as they are (retain the $ symbols).
   - Part 2 [Translation]: the corresponding literal Chinese translation (used to check whether the logic matches the original meaning).
   - Apart from these two parts, do not output any extra dialogue or explanation.

# Execution Protocol
Before outputting the final result, be sure to self-review in the background:
1.…
```

# Vex · 维刻

Write down your ideas, see their structure.

Vex is a desktop Markdown editor built on .NET 10 and Avalonia 12. It supports **Windows, Linux, and macOS**, and centers on local files with instant editing, source view, reading, chapter mind maps, export, and local MCP collaboration.

Official site: [vex.codewf.com](https://vex.codewf.com/) · Published by [码坊 CodeWF](https://codewf.com) · Current version: **1.7.3**

Download the installers and their SHA256 checksums from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/dotnet9/Vex/releases/latest): Windows x64 EXE, Linux x64/arm64 DEB, and macOS x64/arm64 DMG.

- Instant editing, source, reading, and chapter mind maps, with eight fixed layouts and standalone view windows that share the current document.
- Local files and folders, recent history, outline, find and replace, auto-save, and draft recovery.
- Export to Markdown, HTML, PDF, PNG, and Word; copy to WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and 稀土掘金.

# Jason Tools Document Toolbox v1.17.20

> ### ⚠ If you installed via git before 2026-09-13, run one line before upgrading to this version
>
> This project rewrote its git history on 2026-09-13 (removing data that was accidentally committed), and all tags now point to new commits. **The old `jtdt update` fails at the `git fetch --tags` step with "`would clobber existing tag`"**, and the message only says `git fetch failed`, which doesn't reveal that tags are the cause. Run the line below once to fix this permanently:
>
> ```bash
> # Linux / macOS
> sudo git -C /opt/jt-doc-tools fetch --tags --force origin
> # Windows (run PowerShell as Administrator)
> git -C "C:\\Program Files\\jt-doc-tools" fetch --tags --force origin
> ```
>
> **`-C` must be uppercase.** Typing lowercase `git -c /opt/jt-doc-tools/ …` produces "`fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git`". Lowercase `-c` is a **config** option (`-c key=value`), so git does not change into that directory and instead looks for `.git` in your current location. That message **looks like "the install directory is not a git install," but it's really just a one-letter typo** (reported by a customer on 2026-09-14).

> After that, `jtdt update` works normally. **Not affected:** tarball installs, the Windows installer, and installs made after 2026-09-13. This has been fixed since v1.15.43 and will no longer happen.

meat-daemon-404/runspoof.body:
# RunSpoof · Campus Run Location and Gait Simulation

An **LSPosed module** that provides adjustable location and gait simulation for university "campus running / sunshine morning run" apps (primarily targeting *运动世界校园* `com.zjwh.android_wh_physicalfitness`), along with a complete map point-selection interface.

The project itself is **a record of pitfalls**. Its core value lies not in the amount of code but in the "why it can't be written that way" notes in `docs/`. Each of them was settled only after something actually crashed, was judged invalid, or failed silently.

> **Compliance notice**
> This repository is released under **GPL-3.0** and references the implementation ideas of [LocationSpoofer](https://github.com/SuseOAA/LocationSpoofer) (GPL-3.0, Copyright (C) 2026 SuseOAA). See [LICENSE](https://github.com/meat-daemon-404/runspoof/blob/HEAD/LICENSE) and [NOTICE](https://github.com/meat-daemon-404/runspoof/blob/HEAD/NOTICE).
> The repository **does not include** any third-party APKs, LSPosed manager/daemon binaries, or signing keys.
> Using this module to modify exercise data may violate your school's academic integrity rules and the target app's terms of service. The repository author is not responsible for any consequences arising from its use. Use it only on **devices and accounts you own or are authorized to use**, and only for **technical research and self-testing**.

---

## What it solves

Students' typical need is usually "I don't want to run laps on the track, but I want my records to look normal." Changing GPS directly is not enough. The judgment chain of campus running apps goes far beyond coordinates:

| Judgment dimension | What the app actually uses | Result of only changing coordinates |
|---|---|---|
| Location | System `LocationManager` + GNSS (the AMap SDK in the app is only used to **draw maps**, not for positioning) | Changing the coordinates once does nothing, because it keeps receiving callbacks |
| Distance | Point-by-point accumulation via `Location.distanceTo()` | Both sides get the same coordinates at the same moment → always 0 |
| Steps | Peak count of accelerometer waveform (sampling ≈15 Hz) | A 1 Hz push cannot reconstruct a 2.75 Hz gait → cadence 0 |
| Pace | Server independently recalculates using the `SpeedPerTenSec` sequence | Speed inconsistent with the track is flagged as abnormal |
| Validity | Four-point scoring via `isValidPoint` in `libswsport.so` | Spoofing only coordinates leaves scoring dimensions missing |

molimao/iota.body:
# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

**[Official site](https://iotahome.site) · [My Devices](https://iotahome.site/zh/devices) · [IOTA Lookup](https://iotahome.site/zh/app) · [Network Status](https://iotahome.site/zh/network) · [Blog](https://iotahome.site/zh/blog) · [English](https://iotahome.site/en)**

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

The screenshot shows miner distribution and network capacity; the figures are official data as of when the screenshot was taken.

## Features

- **Multi-device monitoring**: add, name, and view devices by public Miner ID, filtering by contributing, waiting for tasks, needs checking, and pending confirmation.
- **Earnings records**: today, cumulative, paid, pending payment, frozen, and minimum payment amounts; also shows USD valuations with source and timestamp.
- **Training history**: view training tokens, throughput, and cumulative tokens by day, week, or month; missing data is left as gaps.
- **Network visualization**: regional distribution donut chart, miner count rankings, slot occupancy, task progress, and tier overview.

# AmneziaWG 2.0-3.1 OpenWRT 
- **awg 3.1 from version 25.12.5** and above.
- Also in release 24.10.8_**v3** but **without the Go module**
+ 
+ awg-go does not build on unsupported architectures (archives smaller than 1 MB).
+ 
+ Two installation/operation options, via kmod-amneziawg and amneziawg-go
  - if kmod-amneziawg is installed, it becomes the priority and launch goes through it, even when awg-go is present. (this is specified in amneziawg-tools)
+ 
+ Via amneziawg-go, it consumes much more RAM and requires a high-performance CPU for good network speed.
  - On a standard router it shows low speed figures.
  - (RAM consumption is 10-60 MB per running interface. The better the CPU and the traffic volume, the more it uses)
+
+ **kmod-amneziawg will not install on "custom" firmware. Only on the official vanilla wrt**
  - The other ipk packages are tied only to the CPU architecture.
  - If you use it via awg-go, it can **in theory** be installed on any build.
  - (use MTU= **1280**)
+
+ You must remove old Amnezia packages before installing new ones. This is critical.
+ Also be sure to clear the browser cache so the new awg. interface displays correctly

A lightweight multi-function system for the **ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75C** round AMOLED development board. The project is built mainly on ESP-IDF firmware, providing a round-screen launcher, watch faces and lock screen, network and sensor tools, audio, mini games, BLE digital twin, and dual-partition cloud OTA.

**Current stable release: [v1.8](https://github.com/soBigRice/soRound_os/releases/tag/v1.8).**
Features released in beta.38 are promoted to the stable release; the stable and beta OTA channels are updated together. Devices with the dual 8MiB layout can check for updates without enabling the test channel.
62 watch faces in five groups, 32 of which are new in this release; STUDIO has 41 in total and uses a pure black background. Existing watch face IDs and saved selections are preserved, and a standalone watch face app is added. The update also includes fixes for repeated drawing in the remote console, sound capsule, and maze, frequency boosting during drawing, and background saving of settings, ecosystem tank growth, and focus preferences. Operations not yet written to flash may be lost during a sudden power loss; no real-device frame rate or power consumption improvement is claimed based on host testing.
This release does not include the map app. It requires dual 8MiB app slots; recording storage still needs separate initialization, and regular OTA does not migrate or format partitions. This release has not performed device installation, partition migration, or device acceptance; earlier device records for local candidates do not mean this public package has been installed. For release checks and distribution results, see the [release notes](https://github.com/soBigRice/soRound_os/blob/HEAD/GeekTool-IDF/RELEASE_NOTES.md) and [release record](https://github.com/soBigRice/soRound_os/blob/HEAD/GeekTool-IDF/PORTING_NOTES.md).

ysicing/XStats.description: Lightweight native macOS menu bar system monitor: CPU, GPU, memory, network, temperature, with fan control, AI usage, speed test and disk cleanup.
ysicing/XStats.body:
# XStats

**Mac system monitoring and everyday tools, with both a main window and a menu bar experience.**

CPU, memory, network, and temperature are visible at a glance. Expand to see trends and per-app usage. AI, calendar, fan control, and other tools can be enabled as needed.

[Download latest version](https://github.com/ysicing/xstats/releases) · [Features](#功能) · [Installation](#安装) · [Data & Privacy](#数据与隐私) · [Changelog](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)

 Simplified Chinese · [English](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) · [Japanese](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/README.ja.md) · [Korean](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/README.ko.md)

## Features

XStats is natively developed with Swift, AppKit, and SwiftUI. It is free and open source, and requires no account registration.

### Menu bar layout

Metrics can be **shown independently**, use **aggregate mode**, or be combined into a single **three-in-one icon** with freely arranged content. In icon-only mode, the Dock icon shows the same live status. Displayed items, order, and styles (text, icon, ring, progress bar, history chart) are all customizable.

Aggregate mode lets you separately choose which items appear in the menu bar and in the status overview. In the overview, you can view metrics together and open details.

The menu bar layout and status overview use demo data, so you can preview different layouts and combinations of information.

### On-demand enabling and menu bar display

In 'Settings → Features,' basic monitoring and optional features are managed separately.

- **Basic monitoring**: CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, energy, and fan can each be turned off. When turned off, live collection, related alerts, and new history records stop. Basic information, page entries, and existing history are kept. Desktop widgets continue to refresh independently.
- **Menu bar display**: Except for the battery info entry, checking 'Show in menu bar' for basic monitoring, AI, and audio also enables the corresponding feature. Unchecking it only removes the entry and does not turn the feature off. AI and audio also have their own separate display options.
- **Display parameter control**: Only controls reading and writing of brightness, contrast, and volume. When turned off, you can still view display information and separately choose whether to show it in the menu bar.

### System monitoring

| Module | Content |
|---|---|
| **CPU** | User / system / idle usage, per-core and core-group load, load average, frequency and temperature, thermal pressure hints |
| **GPU** | Graphics load, core count, temperature and power |
| **Memory** | Memory pressure, app / compressed / cache breakdown, swap space and swap-in/swap-out rates |
| **Disk** | Capacity, read/write rates, per-app read/write ranking, SMART health info |
|…
